messages:
Bob (Acme): Hey team — hitting an issue where streaming responses via SSE get cut off mid-stream. Last chunk never arrives and clients see incomplete JSON. Happened across a few users since yesterday.

Alice (Support): Sorry to hear that. Can you share a minimal repro and the exact headers you use? Is this via our hosted API or Dedicated?

Bob (Acme): Hosted API in us-west. Repro steps:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate" -d '{"prompt":"repeat a lot","max_tokens":200}'
2) Client reads SSE events. After ~1-3s the stream ends with no "[DONE]" or finish_reason. Some responses end mid-JSON.

Here's a captured tail (I've replaced token):
```
event: message
data: {\"id\":\"abc123\",\"object\":\"text_chunk\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"... continues ...\"}}]\n\\n
event: message
data: {\"id\":\"abc123\",\"object\":\"text_chunk\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"final sentence\"}}],\"finish_reason\"
```
Note the stream cut off right after "finish_reason" and there's no following value or closing braces.

Alice (Support): This looks like a TCP-level disconnect / gateway buffer flush. Can you paste response headers from curl (use -i) and any proxy between your clients and the internet? Also what client lib are you using (EventSource, fetch, custom)?

Bob (Acme): Using node-fetch with EventSource polyfill on Heroku. No extra proxy other than Heroku router. curl -i output:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
cache-control: no-cache
x-request-id: r-789

[stream body ...]
```

Also seeing occasional 502s in their app logs concurrent with the truncated streams.

Alice (Support): Thanks. Tagging Carl + Dana to investigate potential reconnect/timeouts at edge or our keepalive. @Carl can you grep for r-789 in logs and see if there was a socket reset or 502 from the gateway around 2025-12-02T14:02:10Z?

Carl (Eng): On it. I see multiple connections for that x-request-id. Early look shows upstream returned 200 but NGINX/gateway logged 'client prematurely closed connection' and then a 502 for a follow-up request. Attaching sanitized proxy log snippet:
```
2025-12-02T14:02:09Z r-789 GET /v1/stream/generate 200 - 0.31s "-"
2025-12-02T14:02:10Z r-789 proxy: client prematurely closed connection
2025-12-02T14:02:10Z r-789 GET /v1/stream/generate 502 - 0.02s "-"
```

Carl (Eng): That explains mid-stream cutoffs — client side is closing socket or Heroku is timing out idle chunk streams. Heroku router has a 55s idle timeout sometimes; but these cutoffs were within 3s. Could be our underlying runtime sending large chunks that client or Heroku misinterprets.

Dana (SRE): I'm checking keepalive and chunk sizes. Also looking into whether our runtime sometimes writes partial JSON chunks without flushing final bytes when a connection is recycled. Can you repro with curl staying open and streaming body to a file? Also try adding `Connection: keep-alive` and `X-Stream-Chunked: 1` (just to test) and see behavior.

Bob (Acme): I tried with long polling and direct TCP capture. On one trace the TCP FIN came from Heroku side right after the last chunk's TCP segment. Not from our client. I'll upload the pcap to the shared folder.

Alice (Support): Thanks. For now as a mitigation: we recommend clients buffer chunks and tolerate missing finish_reason by treating the stream close as implicit finish if the last chunk forms valid JSON. We're also advising transient retry with idempotency where possible.

Carl (Eng): Root cause hypothesis: our server occasionally emits a chunk that leaves the JSON object open (e.g., writing '"finish_reason"' then gets preempted by goroutine scheduling) due to buffer boundaries. Runtime fix: ensure each SSE event is written atomically and flushed, and set Content-Length for final event or send explicit [DONE] sentinel before closing socket.

Dana (SRE): Rolling a small fix to ensure final event is double-flushed and we set server-side keepalives to 15s. Will deploy to canary in us-west in 10m. @Bob we'll ping when live.

reliability-bot: canary deploy started: canary-2025-12-02-1432 -> us-west (3 instances)

Carl (Eng): Added extra logging to serialize outgoing SSE writes and detect writes that were half-sent. If we find >0 occurrences in the canary we'll rollback.

Bob (Acme): Thanks team, appreciate the quick triage. Will test once you say it's live and post results. For my app we patched the EventSource polyfill to buffer until closing brace and that reduced incidents.

Alice (Support): Closing loop: please update this thread with verification result; we'll keep it open until canary is healthy for 24h or you confirm resolved.

(edited to add curl -N suggestion and pcap link)
